executive_assessment.text: Local vulnerability includes coastal flood and erosion records, Amazon/coastal poverty sensitivity, and named provinces facing overlapping protection and service needs.

A conditional reverse mechanism connects documented insecurity-related access barriers to response in territories also affected by climate disasters. It does not establish that a named adaptation project stopped.

Basin-specific agricultural recommendations are distinguished from delivery. Dated food-security forecasts emphasize violence-related purchasing-power loss and compounding weather, without attributing violence to climate.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-09 reports: Twenty of 24 recorded heavy-rain flood disasters since 1992 affected a coastal province; erosion was highest in El Oro, Esmeraldas and Guayas.
Source dated 2026-05-18 reports: OCHA estimates 1.91 million people need assistance in ten priority provinces, concentrated in high-severity areas with simultaneous deprivations.

Source dated 2026-05-18 reports: Armed violence and criminal territorial control drive displacement, threats, extortion and service restrictions in coastal Guayas, Esmeraldas, Los Ríos, urban corridors and border zones.
Source dated 2026-05-29 reports: FEWS projects violence-driven food insecurity, compounded by weather, among poor informal workers, displaced people, migrants and coastal fishers.
Source dated 2026-05-29 reports: Above-average heat may reduce irrigated second-season yields, while poor agricultural laborers face reduced work and income opportunities in coastal provinces.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 12 of 12 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
ECU is absent from EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json and no countries/ECU baseline dossier was present; this is a new-country extraction, not an extension of an existing record.

No reviewed source establishes that climate change caused criminal violence in Ecuador. The OCHA and FEWS NET reports explicitly describe interacting or compounding shocks, while the CCDR documents social-protest effects on climate-policy implementation.

OCHA’s accessible publication-page text summarizes the shock analysis; its linked PDF was not opened. The official National Adaptation Plan returned HTTP 502, the Second NDC PDF exceeded reader limits, and the IMF report page returned HTTP 403.

Security restrictions are documented as constraints on humanitarian operations and market access; the reviewed sources do not identify a specific climate-adaptation project that was suspended by insecurity.
FEWS NET’s June–December 2026 projections were published in May 2026; they are dated outlook estimates, not observed outcomes or a current post-May update.
OCHA's official summary supports a conditional reverse operational mechanism, but no named climate-adaptation project suspension or quantified climate-response effect was established.
Nonviolent social protest and policy reversal remain institutional context; no climate-to-criminal-violence pathway is inferred.

FEWS NET's May 2026 outlook through December 2026 remains explicitly dated, conditional and unverified against later outcomes; national food availability is distinct from household safe access and affordability.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
